meta.title: Checked lead: the 'deep state' network as DataRepublican and Mike Benz describe it, and its paths to Poland
meta.notes: Leads come from DataRepublican (Jennica Pounds) and Mike Benz (Foundation for Freedom Online), credited on each edge as lead_origin. Every edge is labelled by what the primary or best available source shows, not by what the influencer says. Also mapped: DataRepublican's Oct 2026 'Democracy Files' on ex-USAID staff (Renew American Democracy / Democracy Renewal Group, NSL4A) planning responses to a federal government they might call 'illegitimate' (the clearest 'outlast Trump' structure they name; all claims rest on her recordings, no money documented). Main findings: (1) The US-funded 'democracy' NGO web they describe (NED and its institutes, CEPPS, IFES, Internews, OCCRP, GEC/GDI) is real and mostly on the public record; the money is large but the specific totals they quote are mostly not confirmed here. (2) 'Surviving Trump' examples on the record: GEC renamed R/FIMI after Congress let it lapse (closed by Rubio Apr 2025); EPA's $20bn GGRF pushed out before inauguration, called an 'insurance policy' by an EPA adviser, and still protected by court order (DC Circuit en banc, Aug 2026). (3) Poland: Benz's specific claims (USAID advising arrests, NED pressing for PiS arrests) are not supported by the documents found; the 'stamp out populism' line traces to an opinion essay in NED's journal. The only documented NED-to-map ties remain Wawrykiewicz (fellowship, panel) and OKO.press ($100k). No money from any of these bodies to the 8 judges or Tusk was found.

nodes.label: Mike Benz (Foundation for Freedom Online)
nodes.role: Former corporate lawyer; speechwriter at HUD and in the first Trump White House; briefly deputy assistant secretary for international communications and information policy at the State Department (sources differ on dates: 2018 or Nov 2020-Jan 2021). Founded Foundation for Freedom Online in April 2022. Hired by OMB director Vought as a special government employee to investigate USAID records (Dec 2025). MIT Technology Review found he was paid $530,000 by one organisation in 2023-24.

nodes.label: Foundation for Freedom Online (FFO)
nodes.role: Benz's 'free speech watchdog', launched April 2022; per MIT Technology Review not registered as a nonprofit; an early About page called it a project of Empower Oversight

nodes.label: Internews Network
nodes.role: US media-development nonprofit (EIN 94-3027961). Form 990: revenue $111.3m (2024), $123.9m (2023). CEO Jeanne Bourgault, reportable pay $386,607 + $56,570 other (2024). Says it currently supports independent media in Poland (no Polish project named).

nodes.label: CEPPS (IRI + NDI + IFES consortium)
nodes.role: Consortium for Elections and Political Process Strengthening (EIN 52-1943638); members IRI, NDI, IFES

nodes.label: CIPE (Center for International Private Enterprise, NED core institute)
State Dept Global Engagement Center (GEC), later R/FIMI
nodes.role: Created 2016 (EO 13721, NDAA FY2017 s.1287); about $61m budget and 120 staff; lapsed Dec 2024 and was reorganised as R/FIMI; R/FIMI closed by Rubio 16 Apr 2025 ('more than $50 million per year')

nodes.label: Global Disinformation Index (GDI, London)
nodes.role: Founded 2018 by Clare Melford and Daniel Rogers; sells a 'dynamic exclusion list' to ad-tech firms; funders incl. Knight Foundation, UK FCDO (ended 2023), Luminate (Omidyar), NED (ended 2023), one $100k GEC-linked sub-grant (2021)

nodes.label: OCCRP (Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project)
nodes.role: Investigative journalism network; 2024 budget $17.5m, of which US government $7m (USAID, State, NED); says it sub-granted to newsrooms in Hungary, Poland and North Macedonia (not named)

nodes.label: Stanford Internet Observatory / Election Integrity Partnership
nodes.role: Research group that flagged election-related posts to platforms in 2020, working with CISA-linked election officials; wound down 2024

nodes.label: Journal of Democracy (NED journal)
nodes.role: Published by Johns Hopkins University Press; copyright National Endowment for Democracy

nodes.label: Jarosław Kuisz and Karolina Wigura (Univ. of Warsaw; Kultura Liberalna)
Renew American Democracy / Democracy Renewal Group / Renew to Thrive (ex-USAID staff network)
nodes.role: Network of former USAID democracy staff and NGO officials, exposed by DataRepublican's 'Democracy Files' (Oct 2026). Strategy described as 'block, bridge, belong, and build'. Funding not documented in any source read.

nodes.label: Danielle Reiff (former USAID democracy officer; DRG lead)
Paul Zeitz (Renew to Thrive; NSL4A member)
National Security Leaders for America (NSL4A, 501(c)(4))
nodes.role: Group of retired senior military and intelligence officials (1,400-1,600 per sources); founder Rear Adm. (ret.) Michael E. Smith

nodes.label: Dan Osborn (NE) and Brian Bengs (SD), independent Senate candidates 2026

Benz (Rogan #2272, Feb 2025): USAID/NED tactics targeted PiS; 'USAID advises the Polish government on which citizens to arrest to maintain power'; NED 'pressured for the arrest of members of the Law and Justice Party' to 'stamp out populism'; they backed Tusk
edges.verified: Not supported by the documents read: the USAID Poland rule-of-law programme is $5k-25k civic-education grants that bar partisan work (Dexis APS 2023-001); no USAID or NED document on arrests found. See held_claims.

edges.relation: NED owns and publishes the Journal of Democracy (copyright NED; printed by Johns Hopkins University Press)

edges.verified: This is the likely source of Benz's 'stamp out populism' quote. It is the authors' opinion in a NED journal, not a NED grant or instruction, and it does not call for arrests

held_claims.claim: USAID advises the Polish government on which citizens to arrest (Benz, Rogan #2272)
held_claims.what_was_checked: USAID Central Europe rule-of-law APS for Poland (civic-education grants of $5k-25k, partisan work barred); NED Poland event page; Journal of Democracy essay. None mention arrests or advice to the government.

held_claims.claim: NED pressured for the arrest of PiS members to 'stamp out populism' (Benz)
held_claims.what_was_checked: The phrase comes from a Dec 2023 opinion essay by two Warsaw academics in NED's Journal of Democracy. It says Kaczyński 'should be held responsible' and lists cases to try, but notes PiS leaders' immunity and does not call for arrests. It is not a NED grant, statement or instruction.
